batchReview.title: Record reviewers' approvals in bulk
batchReview.lead: For decisions a reviewer made outside the site: on the CSV we sent them, or on a list they returned. Each approval is recorded in the reviewer's name, for the exact version and text they saw, with this batch, the date they decided and you as the person who entered it. Nothing they did not approve is approved.

noReviewers.title: No reviewer can be chosen yet
noReviewers.body: An approval must name the reviewer who made it. Authorise each professor on <link>Reviewers</link>; they then sign in once and confirm the public wording of their credentials. Only confirmed reviewers appear here.

batchReview.unconfirmed: {count, plural, one {# authorised reviewer has} other {# authorised reviewers have}} not confirmed their credentials yet and cannot be chosen.

selection.summary: {selected, plural, =0 {Nothing selected} one {# question selected} other {# questions selected}} · {matching, plural, one {# matches} other {# match}} the filters
selection.hint: Shift-click a box to select or clear everything between it and the last box you clicked.
selection.approve: Record approvals for {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}}
selection.empty: No question awaiting review matches these filters.

export.heading: Send questions to reviewers
export.body: Download the questions matching the filters above as a CSV, with their full text, key and explanation, and an empty decision column for the reviewer: "approved" only when they checked the answer key, the explanation, the wording and the syllabus alignment; "changes" with a note otherwise; blank if not reviewed. Each file holds at most {max} questions and is recorded, so the returned file can be checked against exactly what was sent.
export.button: Download CSV of {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}}
export.done: Downloaded {file}: {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}}.
export.truncated: Only the first {max} were included. Filter by "Never sent" and download again for the rest.

import.heading: Import a returned CSV
import.body: Choose the file a reviewer sent back. It is read in your browser; only the question id, version, fingerprint, export id, decision and reviewer email of each row are sent. A dry run comes first.
import.read: {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} read from {file}.
import.tooMany: This file has {rows} rows. Split it into files of at most {max} rows.

headerProblem.no-question-id-column: The file has no question_id column.
headerProblem.no-decision-column: The file has no decision column.

record.heading: Who decided, and where it came from
record.reviewerHint: The approvals are recorded in this person's name and shown to learners with their confirmed credentials. You are recorded as the person who entered them.
record.sourceHint: For example: "Approved list e-mailed by Prof. Rossi on 12 November".
record.attest: The reviewer confirmed that for every question they marked approved they checked the answer key, the explanation, the wording and the syllabus alignment.

plan.heading: Dry run
plan.willApprove: {count, plural, =0 {No question would be approved.} one {# question would be approved} other {# questions would be approved}}
plan.alreadyApproved: {count, plural, one {# already approved} other {# already approved}}
plan.changed: {count, plural, one {# changed since it was sent: refused} other {# changed since they were sent: refused}}
plan.otherRefused: {count, plural, one {# other row refused or left out} other {# other rows refused or left out}}
plan.approve: Approve {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}}

confirm.title: Record {count, plural, one {# approval} other {# approvals}}?
confirm.body: {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} will be recorded as approved by {reviewer} on {date}, from "{source}", entered by you. They are served to learners at once. You can withdraw the whole batch later.
confirm.yes: Record {count, plural, one {# approval} other {# approvals}}

done.title: Recorded
done.body: {count, plural, one {# approval} other {# approvals}} recorded as batch {batch}.
done.skipped: {count, plural, one {# question was} other {# questions were}} edited or approved by someone else while the batch was written, and left out.

outcomes.changed-since-sent: Changed since it was sent: the reviewer approved a different text
outcomes.unverifiable: No version, fingerprint or export to tell which text was approved
outcomes.content-integrity: Stored text does not match its fingerprint
outcomes.changes-requested: Another reviewer asked for changes: decide on the review page
outcomes.exam-not-authorised: Reviewer not authorised for this exam
outcomes.own-work: The reviewer wrote or edited this question
outcomes.other-reviewer: The row names a different reviewer
outcomes.not-approved: Marked for changes: record it on the review page with the note
outcomes.conflict: Contradicts another row for the same question
outcomes.unknown-export: Names an export we have no record of

errors.generic: That did not work. Try again.
errors.network: The server could not be reached. Nothing was recorded.

history.batch: Entered by an administrator on the reviewer's behalf, in <link>batch {id}</link>.
history.withdrawn: That batch was withdrawn: this approval no longer counts.

batches.title: Recorded approval batches
batches.lead: Every batch of approvals entered on a reviewer's behalf, newest first, and every file sent to reviewers. Withdrawing a batch makes all its approvals stop counting at once; the record stays.
batches.empty: No batch has been recorded yet.
batches.exportsEmpty: No file has been exported yet.

withdraw.reasonHint: At least 10 characters. Kept with the batch.
withdraw.confirm: Withdraw {count, plural, one {# approval} other {# approvals}}
